newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp says ready for electronic money.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp says ready for electronic money.

text.p: Citicorp said on Monday the global bank has invested heavily in developing an electronic money system and has filed for 25 patents, although the timing for the introduction of the new technology is not fixed.
"We have a very large patent portfolio," said Colin Crook, senior technology officer and chairman of the bank's corporate technology committee. "We've made a judgement about market timing."
Crook told a Montgomery Securities conference that Citicorp has been developing a patent portfolio for its electronic monetary system (EMS) since 1990.
"We think EMS is the basis for quite significant changes," he said in a presentation to investors capping the first day of the five-day conference. "It's just a question of when."
Crook said the first of the patents had already been granted and Citibank has already spent three and a half years implementing a standard global technology infrastructure.
The bank's technology initiative aims to standardise applications and data to enable an international understanding of price and cost relationships.
Crook said the project is about 75 percent completed and the final push would take another three years.
Crook said Citibank has used various technologies for customers to access the bank through "customer touch points", ranging from automated teller machines and telephones to the Internet.

He also said investments through its technology venture group, such as its investment announced earlier on Monday in Palo Alto-based television Internet company WebTV, were an important way to stay at the leading edge of technology and its application by customers.
"This is the way you keep plugged in to the tune of the market." Crook said.
He said banks would have to decide over the next six to 18 months how they will proceed on new technologies and electronic banking and commerce.
"There is no absolute security, so it's all to do with risk management," Crook said.
"We are paranoid, absolutely paranoid, about security risk," he said of Citicorp.
